meta.title: How an OCI image is translated | ProxMenux
meta.description: From the image repository and its Compose file to a reviewable template, a deployment plan and a native Proxmox VE LXC, without Docker inside.

header.title: How an OCI image is translated
header.description: From the image repository and its Compose file to a reviewable template, a deployment plan and a native LXC, without installing Docker inside.

 A["{{repo}}"] --> B["Compose + README"]

blocks.p: The converter reads the image and the Compose file its project publishes and writes a JSON template. A template with untranslated blockers goes through review, where a curated overlay resolves them, before it is published in the catalog. Only templates without blockers are offered for installation.

items.title: Image identity

items.body: Entrypoint, Cmd, environment, user, working directory, stop signal, ports and volumes.

items.title: Proxmox VE translation
items.body: Resources, security, mount points, devices, sysctls, healthchecks and the adaptations each one needs, with their reason.

items.body: Supported keys, untranslated blockers and the state of each validation.

sections.title: OCI provides the process; Compose provides the environment

rows: Proxmox VE imports them when the CT is created

items.title: Resolve
items.body: The registry is queried, the host architecture is selected and the effective digest of the rolling tag is fixed.

items.title: Download and verify
items.body: Skopeo downloads the image as an OCI archive, and every layer is checked against its digest and decompressed before anything is created. A damaged download is fetched a second time before the installation stops.

items.title: Build
items.body: pct create builds the rootfs from the archive and keeps the official process metadata of the image.

items.title: Connect
items.body: The declared volumes, network, environment, devices and security profiles are attached.

items.title: Console
items.body: The console output of the container is kept on the host, and the Proxmox VE console opens a shell when the image ships one.

items.title: Check
items.body: The first start waits for an address and for the service to answer; a failure is not reported as a successful installation.

items.title: Register
items.body: The effective configuration is written to the instance contract that updates and recreations use.

sections.title: Example: an image with /config and /downloads
sections.intro: A common Compose definition and the Proxmox VE configuration it becomes. The paths the application expects do not change.

items.title: Docker Compose
items.code:
image: lscr.io/linuxserver/example:latest
environment:
  - PUID=1000
  - PGID=1000
volumes:
  - config:/config
  - /srv/downloads:/downloads
ports:
  - 8080:8080

items.title: /etc/pve/lxc/VMID.conf (excerpt)
items.code:
entrypoint: /init
mp0: local-lvm:vm-VMID-disk-1,mp=/config,backup=1,size=8G
mp1: /srv/downloads,mp=/downloads
net0: name=eth0,bridge=vmbr0,ip=dhcp,type=veth
lxc.environment.runtime: PUID=1000
lxc.environment.runtime: PGID=1000

blocks.p: mp0 is a second disk that belongs to the container, named vm-VMID-disk-N on the selected storage. It is mounted at /config and, with backup=1, it is part of the container backup. mp1 creates no disk: it binds the host directory /srv/downloads to /downloads inside the LXC. Port 8080 is not mapped: the LXC has an address of its own and the service answers on it.
